title: Candidate phase of assembly
statement: Let $x$, $s$, $\mathit{pre}$, and $\mathit{rest}$ be Boolean words, let $p$ be an input-head position for input $x$, and let $\mathit{out}$ be a Boolean word. If $s=\mathit{pre}\mathbin{+��+}\mathit{rest}$, then after exactly $|\mathit{rest}|+1$ steps from the assembly configuration in candidate phase, with input head at $p$, candidate tape containing $s$ with its head at position $|\mathit{pre}|$, and output $\mathit{out}\mathbin{+��+}\mathit{pre}$, the machine is halted with the candidate tape unchanged, its head at position $|s|$, input head still at $p$, and output $\mathit{out}\mathbin{+��+}s$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is an input-head position for input $x$
replaced:
Suppose the candidate word $s$ decomposes as
$\mathit{pre} \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathit{rest}$, and let $\mathit{out}$ be a word and
$p$ an input-head position. After exactly $|\mathit{rest}| + 1$ steps from the
candidate-phase configuration of the assembly machine with input head at $p$,
candidate head at position $|\mathit{pre}|$, and output
$\mathit{out} \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathit{pre}$, the machine is halted with the
candidate tape unchanged, its head at position $|s|$, the input head still at $p$,
and output $\mathit{out} \mathbin{+\!\!+} s$; an empty remainder takes the single
final step.
